title: strict_spawn_class frees temp-allocator slices via delete() — 134 bad frees per test run
evidence:
core/growth_test.odin:527-528:
	parent := make([]i32, n, context.temp_allocator)
	defer delete(parent)
core/growth_test.odin:556-557:
	size := make([]i32, n, context.temp_allocator)
	defer delete(size)
Empirical: `odin test core` emits 67× "+++ bad free @ 0x… [growth_test.odin:528:strict_spawn_class()]" and 67× "…[:557:strict_spawn_class()]" (134 total). Root cause reproduced in a scratch Odin test: `delete` on a plain slice frees through context.allocator, not the temp allocator make() used; the codebase's own convention (group_cluster_view_build, core/growth.odin:196-198) uses [dynamic] arrays whose delete frees via the stored allocator and produces zero bad frees.
detail: Every strict_spawn_class call frees slices through the wrong allocator — invalid frees the test tracking allocator rejects, flooding each run with 134 bad-free diagnostics that can mask genuine memory defects. Tests still pass only because the temp allocator is arena-reset.
recommended_fix: Use make([dynamic]i32, n, n, context.temp_allocator) + delete (stored-allocator free, mirroring group_cluster_view_build), or free via free(raw_data(parent), context.temp_allocator) instead of delete().

title: Seed-floor diameter check uses w²+h² but valid tiles span [0,w-1]×[0,h-1] — seed 49 loads yet permanently stalls growth
detail: The check exists to fail-fast exactly this stall (its own comment: "could never be cleared by any candidate … silently stall growth forever"), yet seed_tiles=49 on the default map slips through: after the first vacuous spawn, every window exhausts the rejection budget and growth stalls silently. The gap widens on squarer maps (e.g. 10×10: seed 14 loads, max spacing ≈12.7).
recommended_fix: Bound by the valid-tile diagonal: reject when seed² > (map_w_tiles-1)² + (map_h_tiles-1)²; re-pin the loader rows so 49 rejects on the 40×30 fixture (48 stays valid).

title: growth_groups seed-floor validated inside the map block — cross-block ordering dependency with no structural enforcement
detail: A growth_groups key is validated 100 lines from its block, correct only because earlier growth_groups checks return early. If block parsing is ever reordered, the check silently reads the zero-value (0² < 2500 → passes) and becomes dead stall protection.
recommended_fix: Hoist cross-key bounds into a post-parse validation pass at the end of balance loading, where all fields are provably populated; keep the explanatory comment.
